title: SEO
purpose: When organic sales drop, a site change is coming or a page will not rank, open SEO to find the cause in our own orders and fix what pays first.
fires: the SEO agency's monthly rankings PDF, the traffic screenshot in the team chat, and the habit of finding out about a drop 6 weeks late.
not_for: a store with little search demand for what it sells, or one a few months old, where paid and social will carry sales long before search does.

jobs.job: When organic revenue falls 20 percent in a week and no one knows why, tell me within a day which pages and search terms lost it and the likely cause, so I fix it before a month of sales is gone
jobs.circumstance: Monday, weekly sales review, organic orders down a fifth, the agency says 'it's probably an algorithm thing', no one has looked at pages

progress.functional: know which pages and terms lost clicks and orders, and whether the cause is technical, a ranking loss or the season
progress.emotional: stop the helpless dread of a drop with no name
progress.social: go to the developer, agency or team with a clear cause and a fix, not a guess

jobs.hire_today: the SEO agency's next monthly report, or a freelancer paid to dig, or waiting to see if it comes back
jobs.fire: the wait-and-see habit and the monthly report as the first warning

forces.push: organic sales are free sales, and every week of a drop is lost money
forces.pull: the losing pages ranked by dollars, with what they share
forces.habit: the agency watches SEO and tells me at month end
forces.anxiety: what if the cause is a Google change I cannot fix and I panic for nothing

jobs.little_hire: any week organic revenue falls more than 15 percent, and every Monday

watch.metric: non-brand organic revenue, 7 day versus prior 7 day and same week last year
watch.source: GA4 organic sessions joined to Shopify orders

jobs.now_after: Example. Now: a 22 percent drop is found 5 weeks late. After: traced in 1 day to a theme update that set 40 collection pages to noindex, fixed in 2.
jobs.not_for: a store where organic brings under 5 percent of sales

jobs.job: When we are moving to a new theme, new URLs or a new platform, help me carry every ranking page over and check it after launch, so I do not lose years of search traffic in a week
jobs.circumstance: Replatforming in 6 weeks, the developer has a launch date, no one has listed which old URLs earn money

progress.functional: list every page that earns clicks or links, map each to its new URL, and check redirects and content after launch
progress.emotional: stop lying awake about launch day
progress.social: hold the developer and agency to a clear checklist and look in control to partners

jobs.hire_today: the developer's redirect file, or an SEO freelancer hired for the migration, or nothing
jobs.fire: the developer's 'we'll add redirects' promise and the launch-day hope

forces.push: a bad migration can wipe out years of rankings in a week
forces.pull: a map of every money page and a check after launch
forces.habit: migrations are a developer job
forces.anxiety: what if we miss one page that makes half the organic sales

jobs.little_hire: before and for 8 weeks after any theme, URL or platform change

watch.metric: organic clicks 28 days after a site change versus the 28 days before, and redirect errors found
watch.source: Google Search Console and a site crawl (Screaming Frog, Sitebulb)

jobs.now_after: Example. Now: the last theme change lost 30 percent of organic clicks for 3 months. After: this migration holds clicks within 5 percent in week 4.
jobs.not_for: a brand new store with no rankings to lose

jobs.job: When the SEO agency's report says rankings are up but sales are not, tell me what organic actually earned from our own orders, so I judge them on money, not positions
jobs.circumstance: Monthly agency call, a slide of 40 keywords 'up', the Shopify number flat, the founder unsure what to ask

progress.functional: know organic revenue and non-brand clicks by month, from our own orders
progress.emotional: stop feeling out of my depth on the call
progress.social: ask the agency one sharp question and be taken seriously

jobs.hire_today: the agency's PDF of rankings, traffic and a list of work done
jobs.fire: the rankings PDF as the measure of success

forces.push: I pay every month and cannot tell what it earns
forces.pull: one money number I can check myself
forces.habit: the agency sets what gets reported
forces.anxiety: what if the money number makes a good agency look bad in a slow month

jobs.little_hire: each monthly report and each renewal

watch.metric: non-brand organic revenue, 28 day, versus same period last year
watch.source: GA4 organic sessions joined to Shopify orders

drives.metric: organic revenue share of total, 90 day

jobs.now_after: Example. Now: 40 keywords 'up', organic revenue unknown. After: $38,000 non-brand organic revenue, up 12 percent on last year.
jobs.not_for: a store doing its own SEO with no one to judge

jobs.job: When our main category page sits on page 2 or 3 for the term that sells, for months, tell me what the top pages have that ours lacks, so I get it onto page 1 where the buyers are

jobs.hire_today: an agency adding a paragraph of text, or a freelancer's audit, or nothing

forces.anxiety: what if we spend months and it still does not move

watch.metric: position and clicks for the top 5 category terms, 28 day
